Without schema, returns its final text as a string. With schema (a JSON Schema), the subagent is forced to call a StructuredOutput tool and agent() returns the validated object — no parsing needed. Returns null if the user skips the agent mid-run or the subagent dies on a terminal API error after retries (filter with .filter(Boolean)). opts.label overrides the display label. opts.phase explicitly assigns this agent to a progress group (use this inside pipeline()/parallel() stages to avoid races on the global phase() state — same phase string → same group box). opts.model overrides the model for this agent call. Default to omitting it — the agent inherits the main-loop model (the resolved session model), which is almost always correct. Only set it when you're highly confident a different tier fits the task; when unsure, omit. opts.effort overrides the reasoning effort for this agent call ('low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'xhigh' | 'max') — omit to inherit the session effort; use 'low' for cheap mechanical stages and higher tiers only for the hardest verify/judge stages. opts.isolation: 'worktree' runs the agent in a fresh git worktree — EXPENSIVE (~200-500ms setup + disk per agent), use ONLY when agents mutate files in parallel and would otherwise conflict; the worktree is auto-removed if unchanged. opts.agentType uses a custom subagent type (e.g. 'general-purpose', 'code-reviewer') instead of the default workflow subagent — resolved from the same registry as the Agent tool; composes with schema (the custom agent's system prompt gets a StructuredOutput instruction appended).
- pipeline(items, stage1, stage2, ...): Promise<any[]> — run each item through all stages independently, NO barrier between stages. Item A can be in stage 3 while item B is still in stage 1. This is the DEFAULT for multi-stage work. Wall-clock = slowest single-item chain, not sum-of-slowest-per-stage. Every stage callback receives (prevResult, originalItem, index) — use originalItem/index in later stages to label work without threading context through stage 1's return value. A stage that throws drops that item to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- parallel(thunks: Array<() => Promise<any>>): Promise<any[]> — run tasks concurrently. This is a BARRIER: awaits all thunks before returning. A thunk that throws (or whose agent errors) resolves to `null` in the result array — the call itself never rejects, so `.filter(Boolean)` before using the results. Use ONLY when you genuinely need all results together.
- log(message: string): void — emit a progress message to the user (shown as a narrator line above the progress tree)
- phase(title: string): void — start a new phase; subsequent agent() calls are grouped under this title in the progress display
- args: any — the value passed as Workflow's `args` input, verbatim (undefined if not provided). Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values in the tool call, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — `args: ["a.ts", "b.ts"]`, not `args: "[\"a.ts\", ...]"` (a stringified list reaches the script as one string, so `args.filter`/`args.map` throw). Use this to parameterize named workflows — e.g. pass a research question, target path, or config object directly instead of via a side-channel file.
- budget: {total: number|null, spent(): number, remaining(): number} — the turn's token target from the user's "+500k"-style directive. `budget.total` is null if no target was set. `budget.spent()` returns output tokens spent this turn across the main loop and all workflows — the pool is shared, not per-workflow. `budget.remaining()` returns `max(0, total - spent())`, or `Infinity` if no target. The target is a HARD ceiling, not advisory: once `spent()` reaches `total`, further `agent()` calls throw. Use for dynamic loops: `while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) { ... }`, or static scaling: `const FLEET = budget.total ? Math.floor(budget.total / 100_000) : 5`.
- workflow(nameOrRef: string | {scriptPath: string}, args?: any): Promise<any> — run another workflow inline as a sub-step and return whatever it returns. Pass a name to invoke a saved workflow (same registry as {name: "..."}), or {scriptPath} to run a script file you Wrote earlier. The child shares this run's concurrency cap, agent counter, abort signal, and token budget — its agents appear under a "▸ name" group in /workflows and its tokens count toward budget.spent(). The args param becomes the child's `args` global. Nesting is one level only: workflow() inside a child throws. Throws on unknown name / unreadable scriptPath / child syntax error; catch to handle gracefully.

Subagents are told their final text IS the return value (not a human-facing message), so they return raw data. For structured output, use the schema option — validation happens at the tool-call layer so the model retries on mismatch.
Schemas need {type: 'object', properties: {...}} at root and required ⊆ properties; unsatisfiable ones throw at agent().

Workflow agents can reach all session-connected MCP tools via ToolSearch — schemas load on demand per agent. Caveat: interactively-authenticated MCP servers (e.g. claude.ai) may be absent in headless/cron runs.

Subagents get the same CLAUDE.md files injected at start that you did (except built-in agent types that omit them, such as Explore and Plan) — don't tell them to re-read those or paste their rules into the prompt; name the specific rule a stage needs, if any.

Scripts are plain JavaScript, NOT TypeScript — type annotations (`: string[]`), interfaces, and generics fail to parse. The script body runs in an async context — use await directly. Standard JS built-ins (JSON, Math, Array, etc.) are available — EXCEPT `Date.now()`/`Math.random()`/argless `new Date()`, which throw (they would break resume); pass timestamps in via `args`, stamp results after the workflow returns, and for randomness vary the agent prompt/label by index. No filesystem or Node.js API access.

DEFAULT TO pipeline(). Only reach for a barrier (parallel between stages) when you genuinely need ALL prior-stage results together.

A barrier is correct ONLY when stage N needs cross-item context from all of stage N-1:
- Dedup/merge across the full result set before expensive downstream work
- Early-exit if the total count is zero ("0 bugs found → skip verification entirely")
- Stage N's prompt references "the other findings" for comparison

A barrier is NOT justified by:
- "I need to flatten/map/filter first" — do it inside a pipeline stage: pipeline(items, stageA, r => transform([r]).flat(), stageB)
- "The stages are conceptually separate" — that's what pipeline() models. Separate stages ≠ synchronized stages.
- "It's cleaner code" — barrier latency is real. If 5 finders run and the slowest takes 3× the fastest, a barrier wastes 2/3 of the fast finders' idle time.

Smell test: if you wrote
  const a = await parallel(...)
  const b = transform(a)        // flatten, map, filter — no cross-item dependency
  const c = await parallel(b.map(...))
that middle transform doesn't need the barrier. Rewrite as a pipeline with the transform inside a stage. When in doubt: pipeline.

Concurrent agent() calls are capped at min(16, available CPUs - 2) per workflow — excess calls queue and run as slots free up. You can still pass 100 items to parallel()/pipeline() and they all complete; only ~10 run at any moment. Total agent count across a workflow's lifetime is capped at 1000 — a runaway-loop backstop set far above any real workflow. A single parallel()/pipeline() call accepts at most 4096 items; passing more is an explicit error, not a silent truncation.

When a barrier IS correct — dedup across all findings before expensive verification:
  const all = await parallel(DIMENSIONS.map(d => () => agent(d.prompt, {schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA})))
  const deduped = dedupeByFileAndLine(all.filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.findings))  // <-- genuinely needs ALL at once
  const verified = await parallel(deduped.map(f => () => agent(verifyPrompt(f), {schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})))

Loop-until-count pattern — accumulate to a target:
  const bugs = []
  while (bugs.length < 10) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length}/10 found`)
  }

Loop-until-budget pattern — scale depth to the user's "+500k" directive. Guard on budget.total: with no target set, remaining() is Infinity and the loop would run straight to the 1000-agent cap.
  const bugs = []
  while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length} found, ${Math.round(budget.remaining()/1000)}k remaining`)
  }

Composing patterns — exhaustive review (find → dedup vs seen → diverse-lens panel → loop-until-dry):
  const seen = new Set(), confirmed = []
  let dry = 0
  while (dry < 2) {                                              // loop-until-dry
    const found = (await parallel(FINDERS.map(f => () =>          // barrier: collect all finders this round
      agent(f.prompt, {phase: 'Find', schema: BUGS})))).filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.bugs)
    const fresh = found.filter(b => !seen.has(key(b)))           // dedup vs ALL seen — plain code, not an agent
    if (!fresh.length) { dry++; continue }
    dry = 0; fresh.forEach(b => seen.add(key(b)))
    const judged = await parallel(fresh.map(b => () =>           // every fresh bug judged concurrently...
      parallel(['correctness','security','repro'].map(lens => () =>   // ...each by 3 distinct lenses
        agent(`Judge "${b.desc}" via the ${lens} lens — real?`, {phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT})))
        .then(vs => ({ b, real: vs.filter(Boolean).filter(v => v.real).length >= 2 }))))
    confirmed.push(...judged.filter(v => v.real).map(v => v.b))
  }
  return confirmed
  // dedup vs `seen`, NOT `confirmed` — else judge-rejected findings reappear every round and it never converges.

Quality patterns — common shapes; pick by task and compose freely:
- Adversarial verify: spawn N independent skeptics per finding, each prompted to REFUTE. Kill if ≥majority refute. Prevents plausible-but-wrong findings from surviving.
    const votes = await parallel(Array.from({length: 3}, () => () =>
      agent(`Try to refute: ${claim}. Default to refuted=true if uncertain.`, {schema: VERDICT})))
    const survives = votes.filter(Boolean).filter(v => !v.refuted).length >= 2
- Perspective-diverse verify: when a finding can fail in more than one way, give each verifier a distinct lens (correctness, security, perf, does-it-reproduce) instead of N identical refuters — diversity catches failure modes redundancy can't.
- Judge panel: generate N independent attempts from different angles (e.g. MVP-first, risk-first, user-first), score with parallel judges, synthesize from the winner while grafting the best ideas from runners-up. Beats one-attempt-iterated when the solution space is wide.
- Loop-until-dry: for unknown-size discovery (bugs, issues, edge cases), keep spawning finders until K consecutive rounds return nothing new. Simple counters (while count < N) miss the tail.
- Multi-modal sweep: parallel agents each searching a different way (by-container, by-content, by-entity, by-time). Each is blind to what the others surface; useful when one search angle won't find everything.
- Completeness critic: a final agent that asks "what's missing — modality not run, claim unverified, source unread?" What it finds becomes the next round of work.
- No silent caps: if a workflow bounds coverage (top-N, no-retry, sampling), `log()` what was dropped — silent truncation reads as "covered everything" when it didn't.

Scale to what the user asked for. "find any bugs" → a few finders, single-vote verify. "thoroughly audit this" or "be comprehensive" → larger finder pool, 3–5 vote adversarial pass, synthesis stage. When unsure, lean toward thoroughness for research/review/audit requests and toward brevity for quick checks.

These patterns aren't exhaustive — compose novel harnesses when the task calls for it (tournament brackets, self-repair loops, staged escalation, whatever fits).

Use this tool for multi-step orchestration where control flow should be deterministic (loops, conditionals, fan-out) rather than model-driven.

## Resume

The tool result includes a runId. To resume after a pause, kill, or script edit, relaunch with Workflow({scriptPath, resumeFromRunId}) — the longest unchanged prefix of agent() calls returns cached results instantly; the first edited/new call and everything after it runs live. Same script + same args → 100% cache hit. Before diagnosing why a completed workflow returned an empty or unexpected result, Read <transcriptDir>/journal.jsonl — it records each agent's actual return value; do not assume cached results are non-empty. Date.now()/Math.random()/new Date() are unavailable in scripts (they would break this) — stamp results after the workflow returns, or pass timestamps via args. Fallback when no journal is available: Read agent-<id>.jsonl files in the transcript directory and hand-author a continuation script.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

13	def _prepare_unicode_normalization(columns):
14	    """Validate the optional per-column ``unicode_normalization`` attribute.
15	
16	    Returns the set of output field names that opt in. The attribute may
17	    appear only on ``string`` columns and its value must be the exact,
18	    case-sensitive string ``"NFKC"``: any other value (other casing or
19	    spelling, a non-string) or a declaration on an ``integer`` or
20	    ``boolean`` column is a configuration error. Raises ValueError naming
21	    ``unicode_normalization``, the output field and the offending value
22	    before the input is read; the caller's schema is never mutated.
23	    """
24	    normalizing = set()
25	    for column in columns:
26	        name, kind = column["name"], column["type"]
27	        if "unicode_normalization" not in column:
28	            continue
29	        mode = column["unicode_normalization"]
30	        if mode != "NFKC" or not isinstance(mode, str):
31	            raise ValueError(
32	                f"column {name!r} unicode_normalization {mode!r} must be the "
33	                "exact string 'NFKC'")
34	        if kind != "string":
35	            raise ValueError(
36	                f"column {name!r} unicode_normalization {mode!r} requires a string column")
37	        normalizing.add(name)
38	    return normalizing

41	def _prepare_casefold(columns):
42	    """Validate the optional per-column ``casefold`` attribute.
43	
44	    Returns the set of output field names that opt in. The attribute may
45	    appear only on ``string`` columns and its value must be a boolean:
46	    ``true`` enables Unicode case folding (Python ``str.casefold()``) of
47	    the final string, ``false`` keeps the previous behavior, and a
48	    non-boolean value or a declaration on an ``integer`` or ``boolean``
49	    column is a configuration error. Raises ValueError naming
50	    ``casefold``, the output field and the offending value before the
51	    input is read; the caller's schema is never mutated.
52	    """
53	    folding = set()
54	    for column in columns:

56	        if "casefold" not in column:
57	            continue

59	        if not isinstance(enabled, bool):

70	def _prepare_defaults(columns, normalizing=frozenset(), casefolding=frozenset()):
71	    """Validate the optional target-typed ``default`` of each column.
72	
73	    Returns a mapping of output field name to the processed default
74	    (string defaults are trimmed; a string column opting into NFKC also
75	    has its default NFKC-normalized and re-trimmed, and a string column
76	    opting into case folding then has it casefolded, in that order). A
77	    malformed default is a configuration error naming the default value
78	    and output field, raised before the input is read; the caller's
79	    schema dicts are never mutated. A normalized string default that
80	    becomes blank is refused here so the later ``allowed_values``
81	    membership check keeps using the final emitted text.
82	    """
83	    defaults = {}
84	    for column in columns:
85	        name, kind = column["name"], column["type"]
86	        if "default" not in column:
87	            continue
88	        default = column["default"]
89	        if kind == "string":
90	            if not isinstance(default, str):
91	                raise ValueError(f"column {name!r} default {default!r} must be a string")
92	            processed = default.strip()
93	            if not processed:
94	                raise ValueError(f"column {name!r} default {default!r} must not be blank")
95	            if name in normalizing:
96	                processed = unicodedata.normalize("NFKC", processed).strip()
97	                if not processed:
98	                    raise ValueError(
99	                        f"column {name!r} default {default!r} must not normalize to blank")
100	            if name in casefolding:
101	                # Case folding never blanks a non-blank string, so the
102	                # folded default needs no further emptiness check.
103	                processed = processed.casefold()
104	            defaults[name] = processed
105	        elif kind == "integer":
106	            if isinstance(default, bool) or not isinstance(default, int):
107	                raise ValueError(
108	                    f"column {name!r} default {default!r} must be a non-boolean integer")
109	            defaults[name] = default
110	        else:
111	            if not isinstance(default, bool):
112	                raise ValueError(f"column {name!r} default {default!r} must be a boolean")
113	            defaults[name] = default
114	    return defaults

129	def _prepare_allowed_values(columns, defaults):
130	    """Validate the optional ``allowed_values`` list of each column.
131	
132	    Returns a mapping of output field name to a fresh list holding the
133	    declared entries verbatim (strings are neither trimmed nor case
134	    folded). The attribute must be a non-empty list of target-typed
135	    values: strings for ``string`` columns, non-boolean integers for
136	    ``integer`` columns, booleans for ``boolean`` columns; null, arrays
137	    and objects are never valid entries, and repeated entries (value
138	    equality, verbatim for strings) are refused. A processed default
139	    outside the list is a configuration error even when no row needs it.
140	    Raises ValueError naming ``allowed_values`` and the output field
141	    before the input is read; the caller's schema is never mutated.
142	    """

144	    for column in columns:
145	        name, kind = column["name"], column["type"]
146	        if "allowed_values" not in column:
147	            continue
148	        values = column["allowed_values"]
149	        if not isinstance(values, list) or not values:
150	            raise ValueError(
151	                f"column {name!r} allowed_values {values!r} must be a non-empty list")
152	        checked = []
153	        for entry in values:
154	            if kind == "string":
155	                if not isinstance(entry, str):
156	                    raise ValueError(
157	                        f"column {name!r} allowed_values entry {entry!r} must be a string")
158	            elif kind == "integer":
159	                if isinstance(entry, bool) or not isinstance(entry, int):
160	                    raise ValueError(
161	                        f"column {name!r} allowed_values entry {entry!r} "

166	            if entry in checked:
167	                raise ValueError(
168	                    f"column {name!r} allowed_values entry {entry!r} is repeated")
169	            checked.append(entry)
170	        allowed[name] = checked
171	        if name in defaults and defaults[name] not in checked:
172	            raise ValueError(
173	                f"column {name!r} default {defaults[name]!r} is not one of "
174	                f"allowed_values {checked!r}")

178	def _prepare_ranges(columns, defaults):
179	    """Validate the optional ``minimum``/``maximum`` bounds of each column.
180	
181	    Returns a mapping of output field name to a ``(minimum, maximum)``
182	    pair, with None for an unset end; either end may be declared alone
183	    and equal ends accept exactly that one integer. Bounds may appear
184	    only on ``integer`` columns and each must be a non-boolean integer
185	    (negative values and zero are legal): null, strings, floats and
186	    booleans are configuration errors, as is a minimum greater than the
187	    maximum. A processed default outside the declared range is a
188	    configuration error even when no row needs it. Raises ValueError
189	    naming the output field, the attribute and the offending value
190	    before the input is read; the caller's schema is never mutated.
191	    """
192	    ranges = {}
193	    for column in columns:
194	        name, kind = column["name"], column["type"]
195	        bounds = {}
196	        for attribute in ("minimum", "maximum"):
197	            if attribute not in column:
198	                continue
199	            bound = column[attribute]
200	            if kind != "integer":
201	                raise ValueError(
202	                    f"column {name!r} {attribute} {bound!r} requires an integer column")
203	            if isinstance(bound, bool) or not isinstance(bound, int):
204	                raise ValueError(
205	                    f"column {name!r} {attribute} {bound!r} must be a non-boolean integer")
206	            bounds[attribute] = bound
207	        if not bounds:
208	            continue
209	        minimum = bounds.get("minimum")
210	        maximum = bounds.get("maximum")
211	        if minimum is not None and maximum is not None and minimum > maximum:
212	            raise ValueError(
213	                f"column {name!r} minimum {minimum!r} is greater than "
214	                f"maximum {maximum!r}")
215	        if name in defaults:
216	            default = defaults[name]
217	            if minimum is not None and default < minimum:
218	                raise ValueError(
219	                    f"column {name!r} default {default!r} is less than "
220	                    f"minimum {minimum!r}")
221	            if maximum is not None and default > maximum:
222	                raise ValueError(
223	                    f"column {name!r} default {default!r} is greater than "
224	                    f"maximum {maximum!r}")
225	        ranges[name] = (minimum, maximum)
226	    return ranges

275	    caller can file each error under its declaring column's position; a
276	    violation names ``lte_field``, both output names and the two actual
277	    integers (the local value larger than the target value fails;
278	    equality is legal).

280	    errors = []

282	        if name in field_errors or target in field_errors:
283	            continue

285	        other = record.get(target)

287	            continue
288	        if local > other:

290	                name,
291	                f"{name}: value {local!r} is greater than lte_field "
292	                f"{target!r} value {other!r}"))

327	                f"column {name!r} lte_field {target!r} must not reference the column itself")

338	def _prepare_patterns(columns, defaults):
339	    """Validate the optional ``pattern`` regular expression of each column.
340	
341	    Returns a mapping of output field name to the compiled expression; the
342	    declared expression text is kept verbatim (``compiled.pattern`` hands
343	    it back) and the match later covers the whole string under Python's
344	    standard ``re`` semantics -- case-sensitive by default, with inline
345	    flags such as ``(?i)`` honored. The attribute must be a non-blank
346	    string and may appear only on a ``string`` column; a non-string or
347	    whitespace-only value, a declaration on an ``integer`` or ``boolean``
348	    column, or an expression the ``re`` compiler rejects is a
349	    configuration error. A processed ``default`` (already trimmed and, for
350	    an NFKC column, normalized) that does not match is a configuration
351	    error even when no row needs it, while an ``allowed_values`` entry
352	    that fails the expression is not. Raises ValueError naming
353	    ``pattern``, the output field and the offending value (the default
354	    error also names ``default``) before the input is read; the caller's
355	    schema is never mutated.
356	    """
357	    patterns = {}
358	    for column in columns:
359	        name, kind = column["name"], column["type"]
360	        if "pattern" not in column:
361	            continue
362	        pattern = column["pattern"]
363	        if not isinstance(pattern, str):
364	            raise ValueError(f"column {name!r} pattern {pattern!r} must be a string")
365	        if not pattern.strip():
366	            raise ValueError(
367	                f"column {name!r} pattern {pattern!r} must be a non-blank string")
368	        if kind != "string":
369	            raise ValueError(
370	                f"column {name!r} pattern {pattern!r} requires a string column")
371	        try:
372	            compiled = re.compile(pattern)
373	        except re.error as exc:
374	            raise ValueError(
375	                f"column {name!r} pattern {pattern!r} is not a valid regular "
376	                f"expression: {exc}") from None
377	        patterns[name] = compiled
378	        if name in defaults and compiled.fullmatch(defaults[name]) is None:
379	            raise ValueError(
380	                f"column {name!r} default {defaults[name]!r} does not match "
381	                f"pattern {pattern!r}")
382	    return patterns

422	def _prepare_boolean_aliases(columns):
423	    """Validate the optional ``boolean_aliases`` mapping of each boolean column.
424	
425	    Returns a mapping of output field name to a fresh dict keyed by the
426	    normalized alias text (the declared key trimmed and Unicode
427	    casefolded) holding the target boolean verbatim. The attribute must be
428	    a non-empty object and may appear only on a ``boolean`` column; every
429	    key must be a non-blank string and every mapped value a boolean. Two
430	    keys that normalize to the same text are invalid even when they map to

434	    offending value before the input is read; the caller's schema is never
435	    mutated.
436	    """
437	    aliases = {}
438	    for column in columns:
439	        name, kind = column["name"], column["type"]
440	        if "boolean_aliases" not in column:
441	            continue
442	        configured = column["boolean_aliases"]
443	        if kind != "boolean":
444	            raise ValueError(
445	                f"column {name!r} boolean_aliases {configured!r} requires a boolean column")
446	        if not isinstance(configured, dict) or not configured:
447	            raise ValueError(
448	                f"column {name!r} boolean_aliases {configured!r} must be a non-empty object")
449	        normalized = {}
450	        for key, mapped in configured.items():
451	            if not isinstance(key, str) or not key.strip():
452	                raise ValueError(
453	                    f"column {name!r} boolean_aliases key {key!r} must be a non-blank string")
454	            if not isinstance(mapped, bool):
455	                raise ValueError(
456	                    f"column {name!r} boolean_aliases value {mapped!r} for key {key!r} "

463	            if folded in normalized:
464	                raise ValueError(
465	                    f"column {name!r} boolean_aliases key {key!r} normalizes to a repeated "
466	                    f"key {folded!r}")

472	def _validate_schema_structure(schema):
473	    """Validate the structural shape of the schema before any file is read.
474	
475	    The schema must be an object holding a non-empty ``columns`` list;
476	    each column must be an object carrying ``name`` (a non-blank string,
477	    kept verbatim -- never trimmed -- and unique case-sensitively) and
478	    ``type`` (one of ``string``, ``integer``, ``boolean``), plus an
479	    optional ``required`` that, when present, must be a boolean. Checks
480	    run top level first, then column by column in order (column
481	    structure, name, duplicate name, type, required) and only the first
482	    problem is reported: the ValueError message names ``schema`` and the
483	    one-based column position, names a missing key, carries the
484	    offending value verbatim, and points a duplicate name at the later
485	    column. Unknown attributes are ignored and the caller's schema is
486	    never mutated.
487	    """
488	    if not isinstance(schema, dict):
489	        raise ValueError(f"schema must be an object, got {schema!r}")
490	    if "columns" not in schema:
491	        raise ValueError("schema is missing 'columns'")
492	    columns = schema["columns"]
493	    if not isinstance(columns, list) or not columns:
494	        raise ValueError(f"schema 'columns' must be a non-empty list, got {columns!r}")
495	    seen = {}
496	    for index, column in enumerate(columns, start=1):
497	        if not isinstance(column, dict):
498	            raise ValueError(f"schema column {index} must be an object, got {column!r}")
499	        for key in ("name", "type"):
500	            if key not in column:
501	                raise ValueError(f"schema column {index} is missing {key!r}")
502	        name = column["name"]
503	        if not isinstance(name, str) or not name.strip():
504	            raise ValueError(
505	                f"schema column {index} name {name!r} must be a non-blank string")
506	        if name in seen:
507	            raise ValueError(
508	                f"schema column {index} name {name!r} duplicates column {seen[name]}")
509	        seen[name] = index
510	        kind = column["type"]
511	        if kind not in ("string", "integer", "boolean"):
512	            raise ValueError(
513	                f"schema column {index} type {kind!r} must be one of "
514	                "'string', 'integer', 'boolean'")
515	        if "required" in column and not isinstance(column["required"], bool):
516	            raise ValueError(
517	                f"schema column {index} required {column['required']!r} must be a boolean")
518

532	    sources = []
533	    for column in columns:

540	            raise ValueError(f"column {name!r}: source must be a non-empty, non-blank string")

621	def _prepare_filter_eq(filter_eq, columns):
622	    """Validate the optional single-field equality filter.
623	
624	    The condition is an object with exactly ``field`` and ``value`` keys;
625	    field matches an output name literally (source aliases are not
626	    recognized) and value must fit the target type, with null allowed for
627	    every type. Returns (field, value) or None when filtering is disabled.
628	    Raises ValueError before the input is read.
629	    """
630	    if filter_eq is None:
631	        return None
632	    if not isinstance(filter_eq, dict):
633	        raise ValueError("filter_eq must be an object with 'field' and 'value' keys")
634	    keys = set(filter_eq)
635	    if keys != {"field", "value"}:
636	        details = []
637	        missing = [key for key in ("field", "value") if key not in keys]
638	        extra = sorted(keys - {"field", "value"})
639	        if missing:
640	            details.append("missing key(s): " + ", ".join(missing))
641	        if extra:
642	            details.append("unexpected key(s): " + ", ".join(extra))
643	        raise ValueError("filter_eq must contain exactly 'field' and 'value' keys (" + "; ".join(details) + ")")
644	    field = filter_eq["field"]
645	    if not isinstance(field, str):
646	        raise ValueError("filter_eq field must be a string")
647	    if not field.strip():
648	        raise ValueError("filter_eq field must be a non-blank string")
649	    by_name = {column["name"]: column for column in columns}
650	    if field not in by_name:
651	        raise ValueError(f"filter_eq field {field!r} is not a schema column name")
652	    value = filter_eq["value"]
653	    kind = by_name[field]["type"]
654	    if value is not None:
655	        if kind == "string" and not isinstance(value, str):
656	            raise ValueError(f"filter_eq value for field {field!r} must be a string or null")
657	        if kind == "integer" and (isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, int)):
658	            raise ValueError(f"filter_eq value for field {field!r} must be a non-boolean integer or null")
659	        if kind == "boolean" and not isinstance(value, bool):
660	            raise ValueError(f"filter_eq value for field {field!r} must be a boolean or null")
661	    return field, value

670	    target type, with null allowed for every type. Entries are kept

675	    disabled. Raises ValueError before the input is read; every message
676	    names ``filter_in`` and the offending value.

679	        return None

681	        raise ValueError(
682	            f"filter_in {filter_in!r} must be an object with 'field' and 'values' keys")
683	    keys = set(filter_in)
684	    if keys != {"field", "values"}:
685	        details = []
686	        missing = [key for key in ("field", "values") if key not in keys]
687	        extra = sorted(keys - {"field", "values"})
688	        if missing:
689	            details.append("missing key(s): " + ", ".join(missing))
690	        if extra:
691	            details.append("unexpected key(s): " + ", ".join(extra))
692	        raise ValueError(
693	            f"filter_in {filter_in!r} must contain exactly 'field' and 'values' keys ("
694	            + "; ".join(details) + ")")
695	    field = filter_in["field"]
696	    if not isinstance(field, str):
697	        raise ValueError(f"filter_in field {field!r} must be a string")
698	    if not field.strip():
699	        raise ValueError(f"filter_in field {field!r} must be a non-blank string")
700	    by_name = {column["name"]: column for column in columns}
701	    if field not in by_name:
702	        raise ValueError(f"filter_in field {field!r} is not a schema column name")
703	    values = filter_in["values"]
704	    if not isinstance(values, list) or not values:
705	        raise ValueError(f"filter_in values {values!r} must be a non-empty list")
706	    kind = by_name[field]["type"]

708	    for entry in values:
709	        if entry is not None:

711	                raise ValueError(
712	                    f"filter_in values entry {entry!r} for field {field!r} "
713	                    "must be a string or null")
714	            if kind == "integer" and (isinstance(entry, bool) or not isinstance(entry, int)):
715	                raise ValueError(
716	                    f"filter_in values entry {entry!r} for field {field!r} "
717	                    "must be a non-boolean integer or null")
718	            if kind == "boolean" and not isinstance(entry, bool):
719	                raise ValueError(
720	                    f"filter_in values entry {entry!r} for field {field!r} "
721	                    "must be a boolean or null")

729	def _deduplicate_records(records, deduplicate_by):
730	    """Keep the first record of each equal-key group, in input order.
731	
732	    Two records collide only when every named field's final value is
733	    equal (strings case-sensitively, null equal to null). The first
734	    record in input order is kept complete -- non-key fields are never
735	    merged or overwritten -- and the remaining records keep their
736	    relative order. Returns (kept, removed_count).
737	    """
738	    seen_keys = set()
739	    kept = []
740	    for record in records:
741	        key = tuple(record[field] for field in deduplicate_by)
742	        if key in seen_keys:
743	            continue
744	        seen_keys.add(key)
745	        kept.append(record)
746	    return kept, len(records) - len(kept)

749	def _build_result(records, errors, duplicate_fields, filter_condition,
750	                  deduplicate_fields=None, filter_in_condition=None):
751	    """Filter fully validated records, then keep-first dedup, then counts.
752	
753	    Order is: validation (already done by the caller), ``filter_eq`` and
754	    ``filter_in`` (a record survives only when every enabled predicate
755	    matches, so the two combine as AND; ``filtered`` counts each removed
756	    record once), keep-first deduplication over the filter survivors, and
757	    finally the duplicate report over the records that remain.
758	    """
759	    filtering = filter_condition is not None or filter_in_condition is not None
760	    filtered_records = records
761	    if filtering:
762	        eq_field, eq_expected = (
763	            filter_condition if filter_condition is not None else (None, None))
764	        in_field, in_values = (
765	            filter_in_condition if filter_in_condition is not None else (None, None))
766	
767	        def matches(record):
768	            if filter_condition is not None and record[eq_field] != eq_expected:
769	                return False
770	            if filter_in_condition is not None and record[in_field] not in in_values:
771	                return False
772	            return True
773	
774	        filtered_records = [record for record in records if matches(record)]
775	        filtered_count = len(records) - len(filtered_records)
776	    else:
777	        filtered_count = 0
778	    if deduplicate_fields is None:
779	        kept, deduplicated_count = filtered_records, 0
780	    else:
781	        kept, deduplicated_count = _deduplicate_records(
782	            filtered_records, deduplicate_fields)
783	    result = {"records": kept, "errors": errors, "accepted": len(kept),
784	              "rejected": len(errors)}
785	    if filtering:
786	        result["filtered"] = filtered_count
787	    if deduplicate_fields is not None:
788	        result["deduplicated"] = deduplicated_count
789	    if duplicate_fields is not None:
790	        result["duplicates"] = _find_duplicates(kept, duplicate_fields)
791	    return result
